items.name: Kitchen base cabinet
items.summary: Base cabinets come in standard widths: plan the run around the sink and the appliances first.

items.name: Kitchen wall cabinet
items.summary: Screw it to the studs, never only into the drywall.

items.name: Countertop
items.summary: Order it once the base cabinets are installed and level, with the cut-outs for the sink and the cooktop.

items.name: Kitchen sink
items.summary: Check the smallest cabinet it fits and whether it mounts under or on top of the counter.

items.name: Kitchen faucet
items.summary: Match the number of holes in the sink or the counter.

items.name: Range hood
items.summary: A hood ducted to the outside works best; make it at least as wide as the cooktop.

items.name: Cabinet pull
items.summary: When replacing pulls, match the hole spacing, centre to centre.

items.name: Bathroom vanity
items.summary: Check the water and drain positions in the wall against the open back of the cabinet.

items.name: Vanity top with sink
items.summary: Match the top to the cabinet width and its faucet holes to the faucet.

items.name: Bathroom faucet
items.summary: Single-hole or widespread: match the holes in the vanity top.

items.name: Bathroom mirror
items.summary: Pick one no wider than the vanity and fix it to studs or rated anchors.

items.name: Toilet
items.summary: Before buying, measure the rough-in: from the finished wall to the centre of the floor drain.

items.name: Shower glass panel
items.summary: Use tempered safety glass; a fixed panel mounts in a floor channel with a wall bracket.

items.name: Shower valve
items.summary: Buy the valve body and its trim from the same brand; a pressure-balancing valve keeps the temperature steady.

items.name: Rain shower head
items.summary: Check that the arm and the thread match the valve's outlet.

items.name: Linear shower drain
items.summary: The drain must belong to the waterproofing system used on the shower floor.

items.name: Towel bar
items.summary: Fix it into studs or with anchors rated for pulling loads.

items.name: Prehung interior door
items.summary: Measure the rough opening and the wall thickness, and choose the hand from the side it opens toward.

items.name: Exterior entry door
items.summary: Choose an insulated steel or fibreglass door with weatherstripping; measure the rough opening and choose the hand.

items.name: Door lever
items.summary: Passage for halls; privacy, with a lock, for bathrooms and bedrooms.

items.name: Entry door handleset
items.summary: Pair it with a deadbolt and check the door's bore hole and backset.

items.name: Window
items.summary: Order by the rough opening; a bedroom needs a window that opens wide enough to get out through.

items.name: Window sill
items.summary: Buy the board deeper than the wall so it overhangs the trim.

items.name: Door casing
items.summary: Measure both sides of the opening; casing is sold in lengths to cut at 45°.

items.name: Duplex receptacle
items.summary: Match the circuit's amperage (15 A or 20 A) and choose tamper-resistant receptacles.

items.name: GFCI receptacle
items.summary: Near a sink, a ground-fault receptacle protects against shocks, and also protects the receptacles wired after it.

items.name: Light switch
items.summary: Use a 3-way switch where a light is controlled from two places; a dimmer needs dimmable bulbs.

items.name: Line-voltage thermostat
items.summary: An electric baseboard needs a line-voltage thermostat rated for the heater's wattage.

items.name: Electric baseboard heater
items.summary: Size it to the room's heat loss, not only its area, and keep it clear of curtains.

items.name: Electrical panel
items.summary: Only a licensed electrician may install or change it; plan spare spaces for future circuits.

items.name: Ceiling light fixture
items.summary: Check the fixture's weight against the electrical box, and choose the colour temperature of the light.

items.name: Smoke and CO alarm
items.summary: Hard-wired, interconnected alarms sound together; a combined unit also detects carbon monoxide.

items.name: Bathroom exhaust fan
items.summary: Choose the airflow for the bathroom's size and duct it to the outside, never into the attic.

items.name: Baseboard
items.summary: Buy a little more than the measured length to allow for the corner cuts.

items.name: PEX pipe, 3/4 in
items.summary: Red for hot and blue for cold water make the runs easy to trace; support it every 0.8 m when it runs horizontally.

items.name: PEX pipe, 1/2 in
items.summary: Buy the same PEX type (A, B or C) as the fittings and tools you will use.

items.name: PEX elbow, 3/4 in
items.summary: Match the fitting system (crimp, clamp or expansion) to your tool.

items.name: PEX elbow, 1/2 in
items.summary: Match the fitting system (crimp, clamp or expansion) to your tool.

items.name: PEX tee
items.summary: Where a 1/2 in branch leaves a 3/4 in line, buy a reducing tee.

items.name: PEX crimp ring
items.summary: One ring per pipe end in each fitting; buy rings in both sizes, 1/2 in and 3/4 in.

items.name: ProPEX expansion ring
items.summary: PEX-a pipe such as Uponor AquaPEX is joined by expanding the pipe end with a ring over it; one ring per pipe end, in the pipe's size.

items.name: PEX pipe clip
items.summary: Clips must hold the pipe without pinching or cutting it.

items.name: PEX drop-ear elbow
items.summary: Screwed to blocking, it holds the stub-out firmly where the shut-off valve will go.

items.name: ABS pipe, 3 in
items.summary: A water closet drains through 3 in pipe at least; support horizontal runs every 1.2 m.

items.name: ABS pipe, 2 in
items.summary: A shower discharging 9.5 to 20 L/min needs at least a 2 in outlet pipe.

items.name: ABS pipe, 1-1/2 in
items.summary: For the lavatory drain and the vent; the code allows 1-1/4 in at least for a lavatory.

items.name: ABS elbow, 3 in
items.summary: Use long-sweep bends where the flow changes from vertical to horizontal.

items.name: ABS elbow, 2 in
items.summary: Use long-sweep bends where the flow changes from vertical to horizontal.

items.name: ABS elbow, 1-1/2 in
items.summary: Use long-sweep bends where the flow changes from vertical to horizontal.

items.name: ABS sanitary tee
items.summary: Match the run and branch sizes, and point the sweep in the direction of flow.

items.name: ABS pipe hanger
items.summary: Hangers must not compress, cut or abrade the pipe; add one at each change of direction.

items.name: Shut-off valve
items.summary: Quarter-turn valves let you close each fixture without shutting off the house.

items.name: Braided supply line
items.summary: Measure from the valve to the fixture inlet and check both thread sizes.

items.name: P-trap, 1-1/4 in
items.summary: Every fixture needs a trap; a lavatory takes a 1-1/4 in trap.

items.name: Toilet flange, 3 in
items.summary: Set its top level with the finished floor, centred at the toilet's rough-in distance from the wall.

items.name: Toilet seal with closet bolts
items.summary: Use a thicker or wax-free seal if the flange sits below the finished floor.

items.name: ABS cement
items.summary: Use cement made for ABS; never join ABS and PVC with it unless the can says so.

items.name: Roof vent flashing
